title: Run the autonomous and watch it
summary: Run Pickup And Score, plot the checks in AdvantageScope and read a failing one.

steps.title: Plot the distance to the pickup

say.never: Before you enable, set up a graph. In **AdvantageScope**, type `DistanceToPickup` in the search box and drag **Drive/DistanceToPickup** onto the **Left Axis**. It is how far the robot truly is from the Pickup spot, in meters.
say.bit: Drag **Drive/DistanceToPickup** onto the **Left Axis**. It's the true distance in meters.

steps.title: Plot the distance to the scoring spot

say.never: Now `DistanceToScoreSpot`: drag **Drive/DistanceToScoreSpot** onto the **Right Axis**. You expect the first line to dip near 0 first, then this one.
Choose **Auto**, then press **Enable**. Don't touch the keys, the routine drives by itself. The whole thing takes about ten seconds.
say.bit: Pick **Auto** and press **Enable**. Hands off the keys.

say.never: The first line should fall to nearly 0 (the robot reached the pickup), rise again, and then the second line should fall to nearly 0 (the scoring spot). The checkpoints **Reaches the pickup** and **Reaches the scoring spot** want each line to get under **0.4 meters**.
say.bit: Each line should dip under 0.4 m: pickup first, then scoring spot.

waitFor.hint: look at both lines, then click I did it.

steps.title: Watch the robot on the field

say.never: Open the **2D Field** tab in AdvantageScope. Drag **Drive/TruePose** (where the robot really is) onto the field, and **Subsystem/Drivetrain/Choreo/Trajectory** (the path being driven) too. Enable in Auto again to watch the robot stay on the line. **Subsystem/Drivetrain/Choreo/DesiredPose** is where the path says the robot should be right now.
say.bit: On the 2D Field tab, add **Drive/TruePose** and **Subsystem/Drivetrain/Choreo/Trajectory**. `DesiredPose` is where the path says the robot should be right now.

waitFor.hint: show TruePose and the Trajectory on the field, then click I did it.

say.never: Add **Subsystem/Localization/Pose** to the field as well. It's the position the robot *thinks* it has, from the wheels plus the AprilTag cameras, and it stays within a few centimeters of **Drive/TruePose**. The checks measure the true pose, so a small difference between the two is not a problem.
say.bit: Add **Subsystem/Localization/Pose** too. It stays a few centimeters from **Drive/TruePose**, and the checks use the true one.

waitFor.hint: compare Subsystem/Localization/Pose with Drive/TruePose, then click I did it.

say.never: Aiming matters most of all. Drag **Drive/TrueAimErrorDegrees** onto the **Left Axis**. It is how many degrees the robot truly is from facing the goal. After the second path it should swing to about 0 *before* the shot, and the **Aims before it shoots** checkpoint wants it under **5 degrees** when the shot starts.
say.bit: Drag **Drive/TrueAimErrorDegrees** onto the **Left Axis**. Under 5 degrees at the shot.

say.never: **Subsystem/Shooter/ShotCount** counts the shots. The **Shoots** checkpoint wants at least 1. `AimErrorAtShotDegrees` next to it is the aim error at the moment the last shot started, which is the number **Aims before it shoots** reads.
say.bit: `Subsystem/Shooter/ShotCount` should reach 1. `AimErrorAtShotDegrees` is what the aim check reads.

waitFor.hint: look at ShotCount, then click I did it.

say.never: If **Reaches the pickup** fails, the path or the first command is wrong (wrong path name, no `followPath`). If **Reaches the scoring spot** fails, the second path never ran or wasn't connected to the first. If **Aims before it shoots** fails, the aim command is missing, comes *after* the shot, or has no `.until(...isAimed)`, so it timed out. If **Shoots** fails, the routine ended before reaching `shoot()`. After a fix, press Start again for a clean run.
say.bit: Pickup fails: first path. Scoring spot fails: second path. Aim fails: aim missing, late, or no isAimed. Shoots fails: routine never reached shoot. Fix, then Start again.

waitFor.hint: read the failures, then click I did it.

say.never: Open the lesson chip and press **Verify**. The four run checkpoints read the best the robot did since you pressed Start, so one good run is enough.
say.bit: Press **Verify**. One good run since Start is enough.
